reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 the minimum and maximum record sizes of a report file are those in force when the file is created (OPEN OUTPUT, or OPEN EXTEND of an unavailable optional file) and an OPEN EXTEND must not change them: the processor keeps the creation's sizes, and a program that opens the file under other sizes violates the rule, detected only where the implementor validates that fixed attribute (GR6).

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.IoStatusValuesOutside1985Lists: at 85 the status the program sees is IoStatus1985.Report's 1985 value; 00, 04, 05, 10, 35 are the same values at both editions

reader.edition-search: grep -n -E 'Dialect|Edition|CobolVersion' over FileConnector.cs, SequentialConnector.cs, FileRegistry.cs, FixedFileAttributes.cs, KeyedConnector.cs: the fixed-attribute validation (FixedAttributeConflict, Conflicts) and the sequential OPEN EXTEND path take no edition; the edition arms found are the 1985 status mapping, the sharing facility and the LINAGE open refusal, none of which touch record sizes.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the record sizes and the validated set (DOC-A.1-129) are one determination at every edition; only the I-O status vocabulary is edition-mapped.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers OPEN OUTPUT then OPEN EXTEND under the same description; not exercised by it: an OPEN EXTEND under another record size, an OPEN EXTEND that creates an optional file, an OPEN EXTEND of a missing non-optional file (probed here).

probes.printed: EXPECT: MATCH (OPEN OUTPUT 00, OPEN EXTEND 00, OPEN INPUT 00, READ 00 x3, READ 04, READ 10)
probes.expected: sizes of the creation kept after OPEN EXTEND

probes.printed: OPEN EXTEND OTHER SIZE 00 (RECORD CONTAINS 20 over a file created at 12); OPEN EXTEND SAME 00; reread at 12: READ 00 111111111111 / READ 00 (line end)2222222222 / READ 04 / READ 10; OPEN EXTEND MISSING 35; OPEN EXTEND OPTIONAL 05 then READ3 00 333333333333 / READ3 04 / READ3 10
probes.expected: GR18 binds the program; GR6 leaves which fixed attributes OPEN validates to the implementor (DOC-A.1-129: nothing for a sequential/report file), so 00 on the other-size EXTEND is within latitude; GR14 creates the optional file, establishing its sizes; a missing non-optional file fails the OPEN (35)

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.4.5.4 GR18  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR18
OK  §1985:XIII.4.5.4 GR6  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR6
OK  §1985:XIII.4.5.4 GR14  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR14

reader.notes: The rule is a 'must not' on the program plus the processor's obligation not to alter the sizes itself; a report file is a text print stream (DOC-A.1-146 (c')) whose format records no sizes, so nothing an OPEN EXTEND does changes them and the documented validated set (DOC-A.1-129) does not compare them. The record sizes in force at a later READ are the reading description's, and the residue of line ends reads as 04, as the witness expects.

refuter.evidence: GR18 binds the program (the sizes must not subsequently be changed); GR6 leaves which fixed attributes OPEN validates to the implementor, and docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-129.md documents that a sequential or report print stream validates nothing, citing §1985:XIII.4.5.4 GR6. Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-245/src/rw_vary.cob at --std 85: report file FD RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 12 created by OPEN OUTPUT (00), OPEN EXTEND under an 8-character report FD (00), OPEN EXTEND under the creating FD (00); the processor changes no recorded size because the print stream records none. A RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 12 sequential re-read gets 39 (the varying-prefix parse of DOC-A.1-129 arm 2, a Sequential I-O rule, not this one). No reading of GR18 found that obliges the processor to refuse what GR6 lets it leave unvalidated. cite: OK  §1985:XIII.4.5.4 GR18  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR18; OK  §1985:XIII.4.5.4 GR6  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR6.
